beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: Take the skill apart and it's a folder. Eight items inside — a RUNBOOK, a SKILL.md, and folders for Android, iOS, core concepts, references, scenarios, and troubleshooting. Claude opens SKILL.md first. Read the file, then follow it. That's the whole machinery — written instructions Claude runs top to bottom.

beats.narration_text: Steps run in order — read the file, run each one as written, return the result. Nothing branches unless a step says so. What they optimized for: repeatability. Same input, same output.

beats.narration_text: The scope is five things, in writing: app, web, or native integrations; engagement context and state handling; campaigns; callbacks; and version-drift fixes. Each sits inside Zoom's Contact Center platform — Claude wraps code around it, doesn't replace it. Ask outside the five, there's no step left to run. They optimized for depth on a fixed list at the expense of breadth.

A dashed boundary line beneath the list, with a faint unlabelled field beyond it captioned 'nothing outside this list'.

beats.narration_text: Here's the carry-out. Build-zoom-contact-center-app doesn't hand you a talking AI agent. It makes Claude build the app — integration code for engagement context, state handling, campaigns, callbacks, or version-drift fixes, fitted around Zoom's Contact Center platform.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. Ask it: I want to build an integration for Zoom Contact Center that handles engagement context and campaign callbacks. Walk me through the pieces I'd need — engagement context, state handling, the callback endpoints — and name the two or three spots where version drift usually shows up, before writing any code. Go deeper: ask Claude what the skill won't do — where you'd have to step outside its five areas, and what that would cost you architecturally.
